title: connection-quarantine-and-bounded-retry-slo-mitigator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: In the last two incidents we observed transient connection failures cascade into retry storms that amplified regional load and caused SLO excursions for p95 latency. Existing circuit breakers were tripping but immediate client retries and aggressive controller rebalances created oscillation. This PR introduces a defense-in-depth change: a bounded-retry window on the gateway plus a connection_quarantine marker and 'circuit quiesce' behavior in the serving runtime to prevent retry amplification and give nodes time to recover.

What this PR does (summary): Add a bounded retry middleware to the gateway that tags requests with a retry-hash and enforces a per-hash retry window and max-attempts. When the runtime detects repeated failures for a connection or tenant it sets a connection_quarantine flag (short-lived) in the control-plane which causes the gateway middleware to fail-fast with a well-known error code instead of retrying. The runtime's circuit_quiesce routine introduces a staggered reopen schedule with exponential backoff and jitter to avoid synchronized reopen storms. We also add an SLO de-escalation gate: if the cluster-level SLO budget is low, the system reduces retry allowances for non-critical tenant tiers.

Why this is different: Prior fixes focused on shedding or increasing circuit thresholds. This change reduces amplification by stopping retries earlier, coordinating runtime-level quiesce windows and providing a small control-plane signal (connection_quarantine) that the gateway can act on. The approach minimizes user-visible 5xxs for low-priority traffic while preserving fast fallbacks for high-priority tiers.

Implementation notes: - Gateway: services/gateway/retry_middleware.go implements RetryWindow and reads connection_quarantine from control-plane cache. It attaches 'X-Retry-Hash' and increments attempt counters stored in Redis (short TTL). - Runtime: runtime/scheduler/circuit_quiesce.go observes repeated request failures and flips connection_quarantine via control-plane API with TTL and reopen schedule. - Control-plane: controlplane/flags/connection_quarantine_store.go stores markers and exposes read/write APIs. - Telemetry: telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml adds metrics: gateway.retry_window_hits, gateway.retry_window_denied, runtime.quiesce_set, controlplane.quarantine_count. - Docs: docs/operations/quarantine-playbook.md describes incident runbook and rollback steps.

Testing and verification: Unit tests added for middleware and runtime quiesce logic; e2e test under tests/e2e/connection_quarantine_test.go simulates transient failures and asserts no retry amplification and that high-priority tier still receives allowed retries. Canary rollout plan uses feature flag 'bounded_retry_v1' with default off and gradual rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor gateway.retry_window_denied and p95 latency. Rollback is feature-flag toggle + revert config in control-plane.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for gateway middleware - [x] Unit tests for runtime quiesce logic - [x] E2E simulation - [x] Telemetry instrumentation - [x] Runbook and doc update - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Canary rollout plan

Backward compatibility and safety: All behavior is behind the 'bounded_retry_v1' feature flag; default remains current behavior. The connection_quarantine marker is advisory; if control-plane is unreachable the middleware falls back to the safer bounded-retry defaults.

Related: ENG-8742, SUP-2119.
